error: The analysis code writes the headline as a literal instead of reading the metrics registry; the number happens to be right.
warning_texts: The headline claim value in analysis/claim_register.json was produced by a literal in src/analysis/build_claims.py:53 rather than derived from metrics/calculated_metrics.json; the number is correct against raw today, but its provenance is a copy, not a calculation.

The frozen check plan has no rule binding a claim value to the metric field its source_value_ref names: claim_refs_resolve proves only that the ref exists, and claims_recomputed proves only that the value matches raw, so a claim hardcoded to a correct number passes every machine check at this gate.

The CLM-REFUND-RATE render roles numerator 27 and denominator 57 are shown on release surfaces but claims_recomputed binds only the ratio; they were verified here from raw (27 refunded of 57 distinct paying customers in the population) and no machine check at this gate holds them.

The refund-rate caveat names the basis as the spec token paying_customers ('unique paying_customers, not order rows') rather than plain words; the frozen caveat topic accepts it and the meaning is clear, but a lay reader of the report sees an identifier.

The metrics period is labelled 2025-Q1-delivered while the spec period ends 2025-03-30, not 2025-03-31; raw_data/orders.csv has no rows dated 2025-03-31, so no figure is affected, but the label overstates the window.

The basis ruling is material on this data: on order rows the refund rate would be 33/174 = 0.189655 against 0.473684 on paying customers, so any surface that drops the paying-customers caveat changes the meaning by a factor of about 2.5.
summary: All five claims recompute from raw_data/orders.csv to the registered values (net revenue 35741.52, refund rate 27/57 = 0.473684 on paying customers, PL 11181.67, DE 11032.61, CZ 13527.24; countries sum exactly to the headline), populations, periods and caveats are correct, and the machine recalc is rooted only in raw. The gate fails on provenance: src/analysis/build_claims.py line 53 types the headline CLM-NET-REVENUE value as the literal 35741.52 instead of reading metrics.net_revenue.value, so the claim-to-metric link its source_value_ref asserts does not exist in the code that wrote it.
